title: Polyglot Resume Surface and Deprecation Mitigation for Iterators
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: High-level PRD: Define a consistent, resumable iteration surface across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that supports pagination, streaming, and safe retries while minimizing breaking changes for existing clients. Deliver a deprecation mitigation plan and adapter strategy so servers can evolve cursor formats and streaming checkpoints without causing mass client failures.
background: We have multiple backward-incompatible iterator/pagination semantics in customer SDKs that make rollouts risky: opaque cursors with no forward/backward compatibility guarantees, streaming responses that cannot be reliably resumed, and inconsistent retry/idempotency contracts. Customers building features with long-lived iterators (e.g. changefeeds, long chat sessions, large embedding exports) need a resilient resume model so transient failures and planned rolling upgrades do not lose progress or cause data duplication.
goals: Specify a single resume token format and downgrade migration pathway that all three SDKs implement

Standardize streaming API semantics and developer surfaces for Python (AsyncIterator + sync fallback), TypeScript (AsyncIterable/ReadableStream), and Go (channel + iterator), including checkpoint emission frequency and resume handshake
Define idempotency and retry contracts for resumable endpoints and provide sample client-side checkpoint persistence patterns
Provide acceptance tests, interop matrix, and migration playbook for rolling server upgrades to avoid customer-impacting breakage
Ship adapter helpers in each SDK to bridge old cursor formats for two release cycles
non_goals: Rewriting server-side storage formats — servers will provide compatibility layers as part of rollout
Large refactors to unrelated SDK surfaces (auth, telemetry)
requirements: R1: Resume token canonical shape — server must issue a base64-encoded JSON token containing version, resource_id, offset_cursor, watermark_ns (optional), and an hmac signature. Clients must treat token as opaque but send it back to resume. Token version must be an integer to allow parsing evolution.

R2: Backward compatibility — servers must accept tokens with older version fields and map them to current internal state. When a server receives a token with an unsupported newer version, it must reply with a clear HTTP 409 + structured error 'resume_version_unsupported' and include a migration_hint URL.

R3: Checkpoint cadence — streaming endpoints must emit a checkpoint token every N events (configurable; default N=50) and force a checkpoint at connection close. Checkpoint tokens are resume tokens per R1.

R4: Idempotency key contract — any request that may be retried or resumed must accept an Idempotency-Key header/parameter. Server guarantees: retries with same key within TTL are deduplicated or at-least-once semantics documented per endpoint.

R5: Streaming surface parity — SDKs must expose: Python AsyncIterator (async for), Python sync iterator that buffers background worker; TS AsyncIterable + ReadableStream helper; Go Iterator struct with Next() and Close() methods plus a channel-based convenience wrapper. All must accept an optional 'resume_token' param.

R6: Resume handshake — client resumes by sending last_checkpoint + idempotency_key. Server responds with either 200 (resume accepted, optional replayed items) or 409 with migration_hint. On accepted resumes server will send a resume_ack event in the stream metadata.

R7: Retry/backoff defaults — clients must implement optimistic retry with jittered exponential backoff: initial=100ms, factor=2, max=5s, attempts=5. Retries for transient 5xx and network errors only. Clients may surface config to override.

R8: Error semantics — define structured error codes: resume_version_unsupported, resume_token_invalid, resume_checkpoint_not_found, idempotency_conflict, server_rate_limit. SDKs must map these to typed exceptions/classes in their language idioms.

R9: Telemetry hooks — SDKs must emit checkpoint events to telemetry (if enabled) with fields: endpoint, latency_ms, item_count_since_checkpoint, resume_token_version. Telemetry should be opt-in and respect PII restrictions.

R10: Adapters/shims — SDKs must include a migration adapter that can decode legacy cursor shapes (for at least 2 past token versions) and rewrap them into the canonical resume token on first use. Adapter must log a one-time deprecation warning.
R11: Documentation — publish a migration guide, API reference for resume tokens, sample persistence patterns (local file, Redis), and explicit rollback guidance for customers.

R12: Tests & Interop — provide an automated interop suite in CI that runs server versions V-2..V+1 against each SDK implementation exercising resume, incompatible-version errors, checkpoint emission, and duplicate-suppression with idempotency keys.

R13: Security — resume tokens must be HMAC-signed by server key to prevent tampering. SDKs do not parse token contents except to optionally surface version for logging. Servers must rotate signing keys with key IDs embedded in tokens.
R14: Performance — checkpoint emission and resume overhead must not increase median per-item latency by more than 5% for typical workloads. Measure in runtime-1.20 perf harness.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Each SDK (Python, TS, Go) exposes the required API shapes and accepts/respects 'resume_token' input parameter in public method signatures

AC2: Automated interop CI runs a matrix of server versions and validates: successful resume (items continue from last checkpoint), clear 409 with migration_hint on unsupported token version, and idempotency deduplication behavior (no duplicate side-effects for retried item with same key)
AC3: SDKs include adapter code that successfully transforms at least two legacy token flavors into canonical tokens during first use; unit tests cover adapter logic and deprecation warning emission
AC4: Documentation includes code examples for persisting/resuming tokens (file, Redis), recommended storage semantics (atomic replace), and a troubleshooting section for resume failures
AC5: Performance validation shows median per-item latency delta <=5% when checkpointing enabled at default cadence versus baseline without checkpointing
AC6: Error mapping is implemented: each structured server error results in a typed exception or error class with programmatic error code property

AC7: Rollout playbook exists with explicit canary steps: enable feature_flag 'resume_v2' on 5% of traffic, monitor resume error rate, increase to 25% then 100% with a three-day observation window and automatic rollback criteria defined
AC8: Release includes a migration runbook for customers and a script that scans persisted tokens (best-effort) to surface tokens that will need server-side mapping
out_of_scope: Large rework of server internal checkpoint storage — server teams will implement mapping layers
Cross-account token portability (tokens remain per-tenant and must not be portable)
risks: RISK-1: If servers do not implement token mapping correctly, large subsets of customers will see resume failures during rollout
RISK-2: HMAC key rotation complexity may cause short windows where tokens issued with retired key are rejected unless server supports key id lookup
RISK-3: SDK adapter shims increase surface area for edge-case bugs — must be thoroughly unit tested
RISK-4: Customers persisting tokens in unsafe ways (e.g., non-atomic overwrites) may cause duplicate processing on resume despite idempotency safeguards
open_questions: Q1: Default checkpoint cadence: should we choose N=50 or 100 for latency-sensitive endpoints? (proposal: 50, expose override)
Q2: How do we communicate resume token lifetime/TTL to customers? Include token_expiry in token metadata vs separate API?
Q3: For streaming over websockets, should we require a distinct resume handshake protocol vs piggybacking on HTTP semantics?
Q4: Do we auto-rotate idempotency key TTL enforcement windows or allow server config per-tenant?
implementation_notes: SDK owners: implement language-idiomatic iterator surfaces and use shared spec tests in /infra/interop/resume-tests. Server teams will expose migration_hint endpoints and a token-inspect admin tool in the Console for internal troubleshooting. Emphasize small, testable PRs: (1) token v1->v2 encoder/decoder + adapter, (2) client resume API surface, (3) telemetry hooks, (4) interop CI
testing_strategy: Unit tests for adapter decoding paths (fuzz legacy tokens), integration tests that spin up server v-1..v+1 in CI, load test to measure checkpointing overhead, and a staged canary using feature flags with health checks linked to SLO dashboards. Include synthetic customer scenarios: large export resume after network outage, long-lived chat reconnect with one-time message deduplication, and concurrent resume attempts with different idempotency keys.
migration_playbook: 1) Land server mapping layer behind flag 'resume_v2' and SDK adapters that detect legacy tokens. 2) Canary on 5% traffic; watch resume error rate and checkpoint latencies. 3) If OK, roll to 25% then 100% across regions. 4) If incompatible-token 409 spikes, disable flag and investigate mapping gaps. 5) After 30 days, publish deprecation timeline for legacy token acceptance and provide tooling to bulk-rewrap tokens for heavy customers.
notes: Keep the resume token opaque for clients; only allow telemetry to log token version. All teams must avoid leaking PII in token metadata. Coordinate with Security on HMAC key management and with Console for admin token-inspect UX.
